transcript.question: Is Cameron Coscia's nonstop waiver churn actually improving The Stinky Faggots, or is it papering over a roster that already had the talent to win?

hotSeat.why: Nina Sharpe is favorite on them (+72), Curtis Vaughn is neutral on them (+9)

sides.mel-diaper: The draft board shows Bijan Robinson, A.J. Brown and Josh Allen were already elite building blocks, so nine waiver moves and 24 dollars spent look like busywork, not improvement.
sides.reggie-banks: Five wins and 1094.2 points with Rico Dowdle and Cam Skattebo mined off waivers prove Cameron Coscia is actively upgrading a roster that would be stuck without the churn.

turns.speaker: curtis-vaughn
turns.text: Good evening. The Stinky Faggots sit fifth in the league at 5-3 with 1094.2 points, but leaned on a nine-move waiver wire this year, most of any team in the league. So: is Cameron Coscia building a contender, or just churning a roster that's already good enough to win on its own? Mel, you've got the board. Go.

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: CURTIS, THE BOARD ALREADY WON THIS ARGUMENT. Bijan Robinson at PICK TWO. A.J. Brown. Josh Allen at TWENTY-TWO. That's the roster. Then NINE pickups and TWENTY-FOUR DOLLARS of churn — Will Reichard for zero, the 49ers D/ST for zero — and Week 8 came in at 116.9 in a SIX POINT loss. That's not building, that's fidgeting. I'll say it: THE STINKY FAGGOTS WIN WEEK NINE ANYWAY, 130-PLUS, and not one damn point of it comes from the wire.

claim.text: The Stinky Faggots score 130 or more in Week 9 against GLORY ASSHOLE, powered by drafted players, not waiver adds

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Cute draft, Mel. Rico Dowdle wasn't drafted by anybody in this room and he went for 32.4 and 33.9 in back-to-back weeks. Cam Skattebo, pick one-forty-six, tenth-best back in the league at 113.8. That's the damn wire winning games. Here's mine: The Stinky Faggots beat GLORY ASSHOLE in Week 9, and Skattebo and Dowdle are why.

claim.text: The Stinky Faggots beat GLORY ASSHOLE in Week 9

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: REGGIE, YOU JUST NAMED WEEK FIVE AND WEEK SIX. Go look at WEEK EIGHT. Josh Allen 24.2, Jaylen Waddle 20.9, Khalil Shakir 20.8 — SIXTY-FIVE POINTS from three DRAFTED players — and the team still lost by 6.1. Dowdle and Skattebo weren't the top line. And this week's nine-move masterpiece? Will Reichard and the 49ers, for ZERO DOLLARS EACH. Nina, grade it.

managerMentions.evidence: And this week's nine-move masterpiece? Will Reichard and the 49ers, for ZERO DOLLARS EACH.

turns.speaker: nina-sharpe
turns.text: Class, the claim is that the wire is winning games. Partly supported. Rico Dowdle went 32.4 and 33.9 in weeks five and six — real. But Week 8's box score shows Josh Allen, Waddle, Shakir combining for 65 points, all drafted, and the team still lost by 6.1. Three games isn't a trend, it's a highlight reel.
factsCited: M20 Josh Allen 24.2, Jaylen Waddle 20.9, Khalil Shakir 20.8, margin 6.1

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Nina, I'll take partly supported and bank the rest. Week 6: 185.4 points. Bijan 35.8, Dowdle 33.9, Skattebo 31.0 — the wire guys outscored the pick-two back's whole afternoon of help. Forty-five point win. And Mel, the wire got Reichard AND the 49ers for nothing, then the roster went 5-3. Cute board. Scoreboard. Dex, is nine moves reported or is that Mel's feeling?

managerMentions.evidence: the wire got Reichard AND the 49ers for nothing, then the roster went 5-3

turns.speaker: dex-alvarez
turns.text: REPORTED. Budget sheet says nine acquisitions, twenty-four spent, seventy-six left. Reichard and the 49ers, zero dollars each. That's the log, not Mel's feeling. That's the wire.
factsCited: B6 - Stinky Faggots budget: 9 acquisitions, $24 spent, $76 remaining

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: DEX SAID SEVENTY-SIX DOLLARS LEFT. SEVENTY-SIX! That's the receipt, Reggie — nine moves and they never once outbid anybody who mattered. Week 8's big claim? A ZERO-DOLLAR bid on Kyle Monangai they LOST to a two-dollar bid. Meanwhile Bijan 21.2, A.J. Brown 28.1 in Week 7 and the team still dropped it by 11.3. Walt, settle it.

managerMentions.evidence: Nine moves and they never once outbid anybody who mattered — a ZERO-DOLLAR bid on Kyle Monangai they LOST.

turns.speaker: walt-brennan
turns.text: This league's record only goes back to this season, so I won't pretend there's an older parallel to lean on. What I've got is this: seventy-six dollars sitting unspent tells me the wire's a hedge, not a plan. A team with drafted talent losing close games isn't a churn problem, it's a lineup problem. My verdict goes to Mel.
factsCited: M20 Josh Allen 24.2 Waddle 20.9 Shakir 20.8 loss by 6.1

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Walt, seventy-six dollars unspent is not a hedge — it's ammunition, and the wire already hit without needing it. Skattebo at 18.4 in Week 7, Shakir 20.8 in Week 8, Dowdle starting every week. Mel, Prolapsed Peehole spent fifty-seven dollars and sits 2-6 at 907.1 points. Money isn't the stat. Wins are. Five of them. SCOREBOARD.

managerMentions.evidence: Skattebo at 18.4 in Week 7, Shakir 20.8 in Week 8, Dowdle starting every week.
Prolapsed Peehole spent fifty-seven dollars and sits 2-6 at 907.1 points.

turns.speaker: curtis-vaughn
turns.text: Walt's already ruled. Let's move it forward — Sam, anything on record from Cameron Coscia about the plan behind nine moves, or is that silence too?

turns.speaker: sam-ortega
turns.text: I checked. There's nothing on record from Cameron Coscia this week — no quote in the file about the nine moves or the plan behind them. I asked. Silence is what I've got.
factsCited: no nonRespondents entry for Cameron Coscia

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: SCOREBOARD?! REGGIE, THE SCOREBOARD SAYS FIFTH. FIFTH! Three teams at 5-3 sit ABOVE them on points, and the wire didn't put 1094.2 up — Bijan Robinson at PICK TWO, A.J. Brown, Josh Allen at TWENTY-TWO did. And Week 8 the bench read 19.7 in a 6.1-point loss. NINETEEN POINT SEVEN. That's not a churn problem. I'm filing a formal complaint about the lineup card.
factsCited: standings: T8 rank 4 at 5-3, 1094.2 PF; T11 1107, T9 1096.4 above/near
M20: T8 116.9 with 19.7 bench points, lost by 6.1
board: Bijan Robinson draftPick 2, Josh Allen draftPick 22

managerMentions.evidence: And Week 8 the bench read 19.7 in a 6.1-point loss. NINETEEN POINT SEVEN. That's not a churn problem.

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Fifth on POINTS, Mel — fourth in the standings, and the three teams above them are separated by thirteen points total. Nineteen-seven on the bench? Moisty Loins left 98.2 on the bench in Week 7 and still won. Bench points don't lose games; scores do. 116.9 to 123.0 against the one-seed. You're grading paper. I'm reading 5-3.

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: READING 5-3?! THEN READ WEEK NINE, REGGIE. The projection has them at 129.7 — LOWEST OF ANY TEAM ON THE BOARD THIS WEEK. Lowest! And it's Josh Allen 22.7, Bijan 20.2, Waddle 15.1 carrying it — DRAFTED, DRAFTED, DRAFTED. Not Dowdle. Not Skattebo. Nine moves and the projection sheet still doesn't list one of them. BAN THIS ROSTER FROM THE WAIVER PAGE.
factsCited: U5 key players Josh Allen 22.7, Bijan Robinson 20.2, Jaylen Waddle 15.1

managerMentions.evidence: Nine moves and the projection sheet still doesn't list one of them.

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: A PROJECTION, MEL? Paper doesn't score. That same sheet had Skattebo at 13.9 in Week 6 — he went 31.0. Had Dowdle at 17.8 — 33.9. Had Bijan at 22.7 in Week 7 — he went 21.2, and the DRAFTED guy came up short. Projections are bedtime stories. 5-3 is the morning.

managerMentions.evidence: That same sheet had Skattebo at 13.9 in Week 6 — he went 31.0.

turns.speaker: curtis-vaughn
turns.text: Projections versus box scores, we've heard it. Nina, grade the new claim: Reggie says Week 9's projection sheet has been wrong before on this roster. Is that pattern real or cherry-picked?

turns.speaker: nina-sharpe
turns.text: Class, three data points: Skattebo projected 13.9, went 31.0. Dowdle projected 17.8, went 33.9. Bijan projected 22.7, went 21.2 — that one held. Two misses, one hit, in eight weeks of games. Not supported as a pattern. That's an anecdote with a decimal.

turns.speaker: nina-sharpe
turns.text: Class, opening claims. Mel said this roster wins Week 9 without one point from the wire. Reggie said The Stinky Faggots beat GLORY ASSHOLE with Skattebo and Dowdle as the reason. Mel's claim: not gradeable yet, that's a future game, but the roster of record — Bijan, A.J. Brown, Allen — is real drafted talent. Reggie's claim: partly supported. Dowdle and Skattebo produced in weeks five and six, but Week 8's win column shows drafted starters carrying most of the scoring. My bias is zero here — this is a numbers question, not a favorite. The one number that decides it: nine moves, twenty-four dollars spent, and a 5-3 record built mostly on names taken well before pick one-forty-six.
factsCited: M20: Josh Allen 24.2, Waddle 20.9, Shakir 20.8, loss by 6.1

verdict.reason: The team's 5-3 record and 1094.2 points trace mainly to drafted talent — Bijan Robinson (pick 2), A.J. Brown, Josh Allen (pick 22) — while the nine waiver moves cost only $24 total.

turns.speaker: curtis-vaughn
turns.text: Neither of you has a win on the board yet this season by my count — this is the first time either prediction gets tested. So let's hear it. Mel, Reggie, last jabs, one each.

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: SCOREBOARD, REGGIE? NINA JUST TOLD YOU IT'S AN ANECDOTE WITH A DECIMAL. Here's mine, one more time: THE STINKY FAGGOTS CLEAR 130 IN WEEK NINE and not one damn point of it comes from the wire — because it's Bijan at PICK TWO, Josh Allen at TWENTY-TWO and A.J. Brown. Nine moves. TWENTY-FOUR DOLLARS. SEVENTY-SIX UNSPENT. That's busywork with a receipt on it.
factsCited: B6 · The Stinky Faggots: $76 of $100 left, 9 pickups
Nina's grade: not supported as a pattern

managerMentions.evidence: Nine moves. TWENTY-FOUR DOLLARS. SEVENTY-SIX UNSPENT. That's busywork with a receipt on it.

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Twenty-four dollars, Mel — and one of those dollars bought Cam Skattebo's roster spot next to a back who went 33.9. You keep reciting pick numbers. I don't care where you took him. Week 6: 185.4, a 45-point win, Dowdle and Skattebo for 64.9 of it. That's not busywork, that's a damn upgrade. The Stinky Faggots beat GLORY ASSHOLE in Week 9, Skattebo and Dowdle the reason. You can take that to the bank.

B6 - The Stinky Faggots $76 of $100 left, 9 pickups, 24 spent
